column1: # required-sysprops.tsv -- system properties the Hibernate ORM suite cannot run without
# WHY THIS FILE IS TRACKED
# `common.args` (the -cp + sysprop argfile every fork consumes) is GENERATED and
# UNTRACKED: each host/worktree builds its own, by hand or from
# `cratonvm-dump.gradle` -- and that dump task only ever emits a raw classpath,
# never sysprops. So any sysprop the suite needs lives nowhere authoritative and
# is silently absent on a fresh host.
# That is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-11 the Azure Linux host's `common.args`
# was missing exactly one line:
#     -Dhibernate.testing.bytecode.enhancement.extension.engine.enabled=true
# and a full 4579-class categorize run reported FAIL=305 against FAIL=4 for the
# equivalent Windows run. 246 of the 305 (84%) were a single
# `IllegalStateException: BytecodeEnhancedTestEngine is disabled` thrown by
# Hibernate's own JUnit extension before any test body ran -- identical on real
# HotSpot, so nothing to do with CratonVM at all. A whole suite run was spent
# discovering a missing config line.
# run-hib.sh now injects every entry here that `common.args` does not already
# carry, ahead of the argfile, and prints `sysprops=N (M injected)` in the mode
# header and SUMMARY.txt. A missing line therefore costs nothing, and the
# injection is visible rather than silent.
# FORMAT: tab-separated  <property-name>  <value>  <why>
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored. A property already
# present in common.args (at any value) is left alone -- an explicit local
# override still wins.
# Dump the effective table with:   ./run-hib.sh sysprops
# Disable injection for an A/B with: --no-sysprops
hibernate.testing.bytecode.enhancement.extension.engine.enabled
column3: hibernate-testing gates its whole @BytecodeEnhanced test engine off by default; without this the ~250 bytecode.enhancement/lazytoone/proxy classes all die in BytecodeEnhancementPostDiscoveryFilter before any test runs
